body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate and increased latency observed for inference endpoints in us-east-1a. Source: infra-health / aws-network / ci-telemetry. Trigger threshold: 5xx rate > 2% for 3m.

pagerduty-bot: Paged sara_oncall (on-call). Escalation policy: eng-runtime -> eng-sre.

sara_oncall: I'm on it. Looking at Grafana now. Can someone paste the endpoint list that's spiking?

mike_rt: seeing a spike on hosted/inference/* endpoints for models: redwood-13b, opt-imx. 5xxs are predominantly 504 and some connection reset. Latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s for requests that route to us-east-1a.

nora_sre: AWS CloudWatch shows increased NetworkIn drop and ENI detach/reattach in us-east-1a around 16:03 UTC. Also observed API throttling on DescribeInstances in that AZ.

oliver_runtime: Confirmed. Router logs show many backend connections hitting ECONNRESET when target is in us-east-1a. Autoscaler started draining a subset of GPU nodes due to healthchecks failing.

sara_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) Pause routing to us-east-1a for hosted inference traffic. 2) Force scale up in us-east-1b/c to absorb capacity. 3) Notify customer-facing channels. 4) Keep owners posted. Anyone object?

jamal_prod: +1. We need to protect Dedicated customers pinned to us-east-1a — will open a dedicated customer thread for impacted tenants.

mike_rt: How do we pause routing? Is there an automated policy?

oliver_runtime: We have a smart-routing policy. Current plan: set route weight for us-east-1a -> 0 and mark as degraded in the router service. Command:

```
# mark AZ as degraded for inference routing
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  https://router-api.internal/v1/az/us-east-1a/degrade \
  -d '{"reason":"zonal network degradation","until":"+30m"}'
```

sara_oncall: Doing that now.

sara_oncall: (runs command) router-api responded 202. Routing change propagated to edge in ~18s.

mike_rt: Metrics show drop in traffic to us-east-1a immediately. p95 for user-facing calls is down to ~260ms across remaining AZs. Error rate still elevated because KV cache lookups time out for previously routed sessions.

nora_sre: Spun up replacement instances in us-east-1b with same instance type and AMI. AWS capacity limited for the specific GPU SKU; we provisioned smaller-scale nodes and adjusted batch sizes as temporary measure.

oliver_runtime: Also toggled prefix-KV cache fallback to in-memory mode for affected customers to reduce cross-AZ calls. Patch applied via feature flag.

emily_support: Heads up, support is fielding inbound incidents from two enterprise customers seeing degraded latency. I posted the temporary mitigation note in the customer-facing status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/171305

jamal_prod: Noted. For Dedicated customers pinned to us-east-1a we offered: 1) emergency migrate to reserved instances in us-east-1b/c (manual), or 2) stay on degraded but with SLA credit. Two customers accepted migration. Opening tickets now.

mike_rt: Quick check: are we seeing DNS anomalies? Route53 healthchecks for some internal endpoints in us-east-1a are failing but resolution looks fine. This points to network path impairment rather than DNS.

nora_sre: Confirm: VPC flow logs show asymmetric routing and a small percentage of packets dropped in the AZ's network fabric. AWS reported a partial zoning event for an underlying network device in us-east-1a. We've opened a support case with AWS (case 1234567890).

sara_oncall: Good call. Keep AWS case link in thread. Can we estimate customer impact? Anyone have count of requests queued/failing?

mike_rt: Pulling totals: between 15:58-16:12 UTC we had ~12k inference requests that hit us-east-1a; error rate for those is ~62% 504, rest recovered via retry to other AZs. Active sessions lost: ~420 short-lived sessions (stateless model calls) and ~37 long-lived KV-backed sessions.

oliver_runtime: Long-lived sessions are the priority for manual recovery: we flagged session IDs and are running session replay to rehydrate caches where customers accepted migration.

emily_support: I sent proactive messages to the two enterprise contacts. One asked for estimated ETA for full recovery. What should we tell them?

nora_sre: AWS acknowledged there is an AZ-level incident and their engineers are working on mitigation. ETA unknown — unpredictable. Recommend we share that we're routing traffic away from the AZ and working on capacity migration; ETA: depends on AWS remediation (~TBD).

sara_oncall: Agreed. I'll put an interim note: "We have isolated the issue to hardware/networking in a single AZ (us-east-1a). Traffic has been routed away and mitigations are in flight. Some customers pinned to the AZ may see degraded service; we are working on manual migration where possible."

jamal_prod: Also flag to billing for potential SLA credits for impacted tenants — record start time 15:58 UTC.

mike_rt: For telemetry: capturing a sample of failing request IDs to attach to AWS ticket. Example header from failing request: `x-request-id: rwd-62a7-9f7d-11e9`. Will attach logs and tcpdump output.

oliver_runtime: Note about autoscaler: because nodes were flapping in the AZ our scheduler marked several pods as Unhealthy and eviction cascaded. We temporarily disabled aggressive scale-in policy to avoid further thrash.

sara_oncall: Good call. I adjusted cluster-autoscaler config: increased health grace period to 180s and disabled scale-in for the next 30m.

nora_sre: AWS updated case: partial restoration in progress; some ENIs are stable once replaced. They estimate the device remediation may take up to 2 hours.

emily_support: Update posted to customers. One customer asked for list of API endpoints affected; shared the model endpoints and the routing note.

sara_oncall: Handoff in 45m to next oncall (oliver_runtime). Leaving notes: 1) router Az weight set to 0 for us-east-1a, 2) autoscaler scale-in disabled, 3) replacements booted in us-east-1b/c, 4) AWS case 1234567890.

oliver_runtime: I'm taking over. Oncall log: will keep router degraded until AWS confirms full network stability and we see normal p95 and 5xx rates for 30m. Current p95 across remaining AZs ~240ms, overall 5xx ~0.6%.

mike_rt: If AWS restores quickly we should re-enable AZ routing gradually with canary weight 5% and monitor for increased errors. Prepare rollback commands.\n
oliver_runtime: Copy. Preparing automated canary script and a runbook entry for re-enabling AZ with stepwise weights: 5 -> 15 -> 40 -> 100 with 5m observation windows.

nora_sre: AWS updated — primary networking device replaced, some residual packet loss. They suggest 30-60m to validate.

oliver_runtime: Starting canary now: set us-east-1a weight to 5%.

(oliver_runtime runs command)

```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  https://router-api.internal/v1/az/us-east-1a/weight \
  -d '{"weight":5}'
```

oliver_runtime: Observing telemetry — no immediate spike. Wait window 5m.

(5m pass)

oliver_runtime: Increasing to 15%.

(15m later)

oliver_runtime: Good. All checks green. Increasing to 40% then 100% over next 10m.

sara_oncall: Thanks team. I'll start drafting the incident summary and timeline for postmortem. Key action items for PM: 1) evaluate cross-AZ capacity commitments for Dedicated customers, 2) improve autoscaler safeguards to avoid cascading evictions on transient AZ faults, 3) add canary automation to router to reduce manual ops.

jamal_prod: Noted. We'll coordinate Dedicated migration automation and improve customer-facing docs on pinned deployments.

oliver_runtime: Final status: us-east-1a routing restored to 100% at 18:05 UTC. No residual elevated errors after 30m observation. Closing mitigation and scheduling postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident closed (severity: SEV3). Timeline & logs archived: https://incidents.redwood.ai/1713054321. Postmortem owner: sara_oncall.

emily_support: I notified impacted customers of resolution and next steps.

sara_oncall: End of on-call note: start 15:58 UTC, mitigations applied 16:05-17:45 UTC, routing restored 18:05 UTC. Postmortem will include root cause timeline and customer impact matrix.

nora_sre: Adding AWS case final notes when available.

oliver_runtime: Thanks all. Good coordination. :rocket:
